question: A 55-year-old woman comes to the physician with concerns about swelling and pain in her right breast. Physical examination shows erythema and prominent pitting of the hair follicles overlying the upper and lower outer quadrants of the right breast. There are no nipple changes or discharge. A core needle biopsy shows invasive carcinoma of the breast. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for this patient's skin findings?

options.opa: Bacterial invasion of the subcutaneous tissue
options.opc: Involution of the breast parenchyma and ductal system

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Invasive carcinoma of the breast" -> "Obstruction of the lymphatic channels" -> 80% CHAIN: "Erythema and prominent pitting of hair follicles overlying the breast" -> "Obstruction of the lymphatic channels" -> 75% CHAIN: "Swelling and pain in the right breast" -> "Obstruction of the lymphatic channels" -> 80%
analysis: The most likely explanation for the patient's skin findings of erythema and prominent pitting of the hair follicles overlying the breast is obstruction of the lymphatic channels. This can lead to lymphedema, which presents as swelling, pain, and skin changes in the affected breast.
